potted plant.title: Houseplant

reasons.cat: Many common houseplants, especially lilies, are toxic to cats even in small amounts.
reasons.dog: Plants like pothos, aloe, and sago palm can make dogs sick if chewed.
reasons.bird: Birds nibble on leaves, and many houseplants are toxic to them.
reasons.default: Some houseplants are toxic to pets if chewed or eaten.

potted plant.suggestion: Check that the plant is pet-safe, or move it somewhere your pet can't reach.

tv.title: TV and Cords

reasons.cat: Cats may climb TV stands, and unsecured TVs can tip over.
reasons.default: Cords behind TVs are easy for pets to chew.

tv.suggestion: Anchor the TV and hide cords behind a cover.

remote.title: Remote Control

reasons.dog: Dogs often chew remotes, and swallowed batteries can cause serious burns.
reasons.default: Chewing on remotes can expose pets to batteries.

remote.suggestion: Keep remotes on high shelves or in a drawer.

laptop.title: Charging Cords

reasons.small_animal: Rabbits and other small pets love to chew cords, which can cause electric shocks.
reasons.default: Laptop and charger cords can be chewed, causing shocks or burns.

laptop.suggestion: Use cord covers and unplug chargers when not in use.

cell phone.title: Phone and Charger

reasons.dog: Dogs may chew phones, and a punctured battery can cause burns.
reasons.small_animal: Small pets like to chew charging cables, which can cause electric shocks.
reasons.default: Phones and charging cables can be chewed, exposing pets to batteries and live wires.

cell phone.suggestion: Keep phones off the floor and unplug chargers when not in use.

couch.title: Couch or Recliner

reasons.small_animal: Small pets can hide under or inside couches and recliners and get crushed when someone sits or the footrest closes.
reasons.cat: Kittens like to hide inside recliners and sofa beds.
reasons.default: Small pets may hide inside or under furniture.

couch.suggestion: Check under and inside furniture, especially recliners, before sitting or closing footrests.

vase.title: Vase

reasons.cat: Cats like to knock things over, and vase water or flowers can be toxic.
reasons.default: Vases can tip over and break.

vase.suggestion: Place vases on stable, high surfaces and keep toxic flowers out of the home.

teddy bear.title: Stuffed Toy

reasons.dog: Dogs can tear stuffed toys apart and swallow stuffing, squeakers, or plastic eyes, which can cause blockages.
reasons.default: Small parts of plush toys can be swallowed.

teddy bear.suggestion: Keep children's stuffed toys out of reach and give pets toys made for them.

sports ball.title: Small Ball

reasons.default: Balls small enough to fit in a dog's mouth can be swallowed or block the airway.

sports ball.suggestion: Choose balls too big to swallow, and put away kids' small balls after play.

knife.title: Sharp Knife

reasons.dog: Dogs may grab knives off counters while searching for food.
reasons.cat: Cats jump on counters and can knock knives off or cut their paws.
reasons.default: Sharp objects can cause serious cuts.

knife.suggestion: Store knives in a drawer or knife block, not on open counters.

scissors.title: Scissors

reasons.default: Pets can injure themselves on sharp edges if scissors are left out.

scissors.suggestion: Keep scissors in a closed drawer when not in use.

fork.title: Fork and Utensils

reasons.dog: Dogs licking food off utensils, especially in an open dishwasher, can be cut by sharp points.
reasons.default: Pets licking food off utensils can be injured by sharp points.

fork.suggestion: Clear utensils after meals, load sharp ones point-down, and keep the dishwasher closed.

oven.title: Oven and Stove

reasons.cat: Cats may jump onto hot stovetops.
reasons.bird: Overheated nonstick (PTFE/Teflon) cookware releases fumes that can be deadly to birds within minutes.
reasons.default: Hot surfaces can burn curious pets.

oven.suggestion: Keep pets out of the kitchen while cooking, use stove knob covers, and keep birds far from the kitchen.

toaster.title: Toaster

reasons.default: Toasters get hot, and their cords can be pulled down.

toaster.suggestion: Unplug toasters and push them to the back of the counter.

sink.title: Sink and Cabinet

reasons.default: Cleaning products are often stored in the cabinet under the sink, where curious pets can get into them.

sink.suggestion: Use childproof latches on cabinets under sinks.

dining table.title: Food on the Table

reasons.dog: Dogs may grab food left on tables, including foods toxic to them like onions, grapes, or chocolate.
reasons.cat: Cats jump onto tables and may eat food or knock over dishes.
reasons.default: Food left on tables can be reached by pets.

dining table.suggestion: Clear food and dishes promptly after meals.

cup.title: Cup or Hot Drink

reasons.default: Coffee and tea contain caffeine, which is toxic to pets, and hot drinks can scald.

cup.suggestion: Don't leave drinks on low tables or near edges.

bottle.title: Bottle

reasons.dog: Dogs may chew bottles or lick spills from cleaners, alcohol, or medicine.
reasons.cat: Cats may knock bottles over and lick spilled liquids.
reasons.default: Bottles may contain liquids that are dangerous if spilled or chewed.

bottle.suggestion: Keep bottles, especially cleaners and alcohol, in closed cabinets.

wine glass.title: Wine Glass

reasons.cat: Cats often knock glasses off tables, and broken glass can cut paws.
reasons.default: Glass can break, and alcohol is toxic to pets.

wine glass.suggestion: Don't leave glasses on low tables or edges.

cake.title: Cake or Sweets

reasons.dog: Baked goods may contain chocolate or xylitol, which are toxic to dogs, and rich fatty foods can cause pancreatitis.
reasons.default: Sugary, fatty baked goods can make pets sick, and some contain chocolate or xylitol.

cake.suggestion: Keep desserts covered and out of reach.

donut.title: Donuts or Pastries

reasons.default: Pastries are high in sugar and fat, which can cause stomach upset or pancreatitis, and some contain chocolate.

donut.suggestion: Keep pastries in closed containers or cabinets.

pizza.title: Pizza

reasons.default: Pizza often contains garlic and onion, which are toxic to dogs and cats, and greasy food can cause pancreatitis.

pizza.suggestion: Don't leave pizza boxes or slices where pets can reach them.

sandwich.title: Sandwich

reasons.default: Sandwiches may contain onions, garlic, or fatty meats that can make pets sick.

sandwich.suggestion: Keep plates of food out of reach, and don't share human food without checking with a vet.

hot dog.title: Hot Dog

reasons.default: Hot dogs are salty and fatty, and their shape is a choking hazard for dogs.

hot dog.suggestion: Keep hot dogs out of reach, and never give them whole to a dog.

apple.title: Apple Core

reasons.default: Apple seeds contain small amounts of cyanide compounds, and cores can be a choking hazard.

apple.suggestion: Throw away apple cores, and only offer sliced, seedless pieces if your vet approves.

orange.title: Citrus Fruit

reasons.default: Citrus peels and seeds contain oils that can upset pets' stomachs.

orange.suggestion: Keep citrus fruits and peels out of reach.

toilet.title: Open Toilet

reasons.dog: Dogs may drink from the toilet and swallow cleaning chemicals.
reasons.cat: Kittens can fall into open toilets.
reasons.small_animal: Small pets can fall into toilets and drown.
reasons.default: Open toilets can contain cleaning chemicals, and small pets can fall in.

toilet.suggestion: Keep the toilet lid closed and avoid in-bowl cleaning tablets.

toothbrush.title: Toothbrush and Toothpaste

reasons.dog: Human toothpaste can contain xylitol, which is very toxic to dogs, and dogs may chew and swallow toothbrush pieces.
reasons.default: Human toothpaste isn't safe for pets.

toothbrush.suggestion: Store toothbrushes and toothpaste in a cabinet, and only use pet toothpaste on pets.

hair drier.title: Hair Dryer

reasons.default: Hair dryers get hot, and their cords can be chewed or pulled, knocking the dryer down.

hair drier.suggestion: Unplug and put away hair dryers and styling tools after use.

bed.title: Bed

reasons.small_animal: Small pets can be hurt jumping or falling from beds, or get trapped underneath.
reasons.dog: Puppies and small or senior dogs can be injured jumping off high beds.
reasons.default: Pets can be injured jumping off high furniture.

bed.suggestion: Use pet stairs or a ramp, and check under the bed before moving it.

handbag.title: Purse or Bag

reasons.dog: Bags often hold gum, mints, or medications, and sugar-free gum with xylitol is very toxic to dogs.
reasons.default: Bags may contain medications or gum that can poison pets.

handbag.suggestion: Hang bags up or keep them in a closed closet.

backpack.title: Backpack

reasons.dog: Backpacks often hold snacks, gum, or medications, and sugar-free gum with xylitol is very toxic to dogs.
reasons.default: Backpacks may contain food or medications that can harm pets.

backpack.suggestion: Zip backpacks closed and hang them out of reach.

suitcase.title: Open Suitcase

reasons.default: Cats and small pets like to crawl into open suitcases and can get zipped inside.

suitcase.suggestion: Check inside before closing a suitcase, and keep it closed when not packing.

cat.title: Cat (Other Pet)

reasons.bird: Cats are natural predators of birds, and even a small scratch can cause a dangerous infection.
reasons.small_animal: Cats may chase or injure small pets like hamsters, rabbits, and guinea pigs.
reasons.default: Cats can see smaller pets as prey.

cat.suggestion: Supervise any contact, and keep cages secure in a room the cat can't enter.

dog.title: Dog (Other Pet)

reasons.small_animal: Dogs may chase or injure small pets.
reasons.bird: Many dogs see birds as prey.
reasons.cat: Make sure the dog is cat-friendly before introducing them.
reasons.default: Introductions between pets should be supervised.

dog.suggestion: Introduce pets slowly and supervise them until you know they get along.
